# An anisotropic strip has a displacement-dependent global depth response

This is an actual planar-fiber, two-integer-coordinate seven-base
response theorem. Its conditional weak limit has an atom on one
canonical centroid plane, while its isotropic volume-scale blowup
is unbounded. It therefore lies outside both response regimes in
seven-base-partial-tail-and-tangent-shape-response-envelope.md.
The additional response data cannot be replaced by constant
weak-limit canonical cap probabilities.

## 1. Exact fibers and statement

Let T=conv(0,e1,e2), V=1/2, g=(1/3,1/3),

    lambda_0=1-x1-x2, lambda_1=x1, lambda_2=x2,
    l_0(v)=-v1-v2, l_1(v)=v1, l_2(v)=v2,
    Gamma=4/9, kappa=2 V (2/3)=2/3.

Fix 0<L<1/3 and H>0. Put c=-H/2, a=4LH, and

    e=(1,-1), w=(-1/2,-1/2),
    E_t={g+s e+t r w: |s|<=L, |r-c|<=H}, t>0.       (1)

The Jacobian of (s,r)->g+s e+t r w has absolute value t,
so |E_t|=t a. Its uniform law is precisely the image of independent
uniform s in [-L,L] and r in [c-H,c+H].
For example E_t is contained in int T whenever

    tH/4<1/3-L,  3tH/2<1/3.                        (2)

At the four binary bases Q={0,1}^2 put T, and put identical E_t
at r_0=(-1,0), p=(-1,1), p'=(1,-1). Their convex hull has exactly
these seven integer fibers, as checked below. Its mixed mass is

    M_t=4V+3ta=2+3ta.

For sufficiently small t every global maximizing point has the
single integer base q=(0,0), and every maximizing selection has

    y_t=g+t v_*+o(t),                               (3)
    l_0(v_*)=a c/(3 kappa H/2+a)
             =-2LH/(1+4L),
    l_1(v_*)=l_2(v_*)=LH/(1+4L).

Write

    L_*=a+kappa l_0(v_*)/2
        =a[1-1/(6(1+4L))].

Then the true global absolute maximum and normalized maximum are

    D_t=Gamma V+t(a+L_*)+o(t),                      (4)
    D_t/M_t=Gamma/4
       +t[4(a+L_*)-3Gamma a]/(16V)+o(t).            (5)

No uniqueness of the continuous maximizing point at each finite
t is asserted. Equation (3) holds for every maximizer.

## 2. A paired-tail density bound valid for every shift

Let Z be a symmetric, nonatomic real law centered at c, with
density bounded by B. For any center threshold q and any
opposite shift v, let its two-tail sum be

    P(q,v)=Pr(Z>=q+v)+Pr(Z>=q-v).

If x=q-c>=0, symmetry gives

    P(q,v)=1-Pr(v-x<Z-c<v+x).

Thus P(q,v)>=max(0,1-2Bx). If x<=0, symmetry instead gives
P(q,v)>=1. For bounded support, a sufficiently large shift
attains one. No common upper bound on a potentially optimizing
shift is needed for these inequalities.

In particular, if Z=r+sigma s for the independent uniforms in
(1), it is symmetric about c and has density at most 1/(2H)
for EVERY real sigma. Convolution with a probability cannot
increase the uniform r density bound. Therefore

    inf_v P(q,v)>=j(q),
    j(q)=min(1,max(0,1-(q-c)/H)).                    (6)

At sigma=0 there is equality for every q. If c<=q<=c+H,
zero shift attains the displayed linear value; if q>=c+H it
attains zero. If q<=c a saturated shift attains one.

For sigma!=0 there is also the density bound 1/(2L|sigma|).
Consequently, uniformly for q in bounded sets,

    inf_v P(q,v)->1 as |sigma|->infinity.            (7)

Indeed its lower bound is 1-max(q-c,0)/(L|sigma|), and a
saturated shift supplies the matching upper bound one.
All laws involved are continuous, so closed/open thresholds
have identical probabilities, including supporting thresholds.

## 3. Exact finite-tilt reduction and localization

First delete the owned fiber at r_0, leaving the six-base source.
For a point y in its q fiber, the exact reduction in
candidate 1ec867c146e96dba,
Section 1, reads

    A_6,t((q,y))=min_(|u|=1)[F_T(y,u)+t J_t(u,y)],   (8)

where J_t is a times the minimum of the two E_t probability tails
at opposite thresholds about u.y. The same single ambient
halfspace supplies both thresholds. A uniformly bounded base
tilt realizes each pair shift, excludes every unwanted core
fiber, and can be chosen to include all of E_t at r_0.
Pure vertical caps are accounted for separately in that identity.

Saturation of the pair shifts costs exactly ta. At every y in T
one canonical own cap costs at most Gamma V, so all local
maximizers satisfy the archived canonical localization:

    y_t=g+O(t).                                    (9)

This is uniform over all maximizing selections and needs no
weak-limit regularity. The maximum and normal/shift minima in
(8) are attained, because the prelimit fibers have full area,
continuous cap functions, and the bounded-tilt realization.

The seven-base exact local identity, proved independently of
any limiting shapes in the seven-base response note, is

    A_7,t((q,y))=ta+A_6,t((q,y))                    (10)

for all y in one fixed neighborhood of g and small t. Briefly,
if a cap fails to capture all of r_0, its opposite core partner
and the own T pay a fixed positive reflected-profile gap above
Gamma V. But the bounded-tilt construction costs at most
Gamma V+2ta and includes r_0. Thus every potentially minimizing
cap fully captures r_0, proving (10). Both local maximizing
sets are in that neighborhood by (9) and coincide exactly.

## 4. All normal regimes at a moving point

For a bounded displacement v write v_i=l_i(v), so
v_0+v_1+v_2=0. The precise local response is

    A_6,t((q,g+t v))=Gamma V+t mathcal_L(v)+o(t),     (11)
    mathcal_L(v)=min{ -kappa v_0+a j(v_0),
                          a-kappa v_1, a-kappa v_2 }.

The lower-bound argument below also applies along any convergent
bounded displacement sequence.

Consider first normals tending to the canonical l_0 direction.
For small t, u.w>0. Rescale by this positive number to U=u/(u.w),
so U.w=1 and U->l_0. Its exact projection on E_t is

    U.(X-g)=t[r+sigma_t s],
    sigma_t=(U.e)/t.

At y=g+t v the center threshold divided by t is U.v.
The optimizing opposite pair shift divided by t may be arbitrary.
Equation (6) nevertheless gives, uniformly in that shift and
in sigma_t,

    J_t(u,g+t v)>=a j(U.v).                         (12)

If v_t->v, the right side tends to a j(v_0) because j is
continuous. This treats finite, zero, oscillating, and unbounded
normal-deviation/thickness ratios without interchanging limits.
If |sigma_t| diverges, (7) in fact gives J_t->a. A possibly
nonzero own-cap excess from the rotating normal is retained
below and never discarded as a signed error.

At the EXACT canonical l_0 direction, sigma_t=0, and (6) is an
equality. Therefore

    J_t(l_0,g+t v)=a j(v_0)                         (13)

with the harmless positive normal rescaling understood.

For normals tending to l_1 or l_2, the coefficient u.e stays
bounded away from zero. Their projected density is at most
1/(2L|u.e|), because the s component is uniform and independent
of r. The strip center is g+t c w, so its center-threshold
displacement at g+t v is O(t). The same paired-tail bound and
a saturated shift give

    J_t(u_t,g+t v_t)->a                             (14)

for every bounded convergent v_t. Thus the two non-atomic
canonical directions have constant response, while l_0 has
the displacement-dependent response (13).

To prove the ALL-direction lower bound in (11), take approximately
minimizing normals along any putative violation and pass to a
convergent subsequence. Their unperturbed own cap must have
volume Gamma V at g, since J_t>=0. The limiting normal is
therefore canonical. Near that normal the exact simplex cap
function is smooth in its point, with uniform expansion

    F_T(g+t v_t,u_t)
      =F_T(g,u_t)-t kappa v_i+o(t)
      >=Gamma V-t kappa v_i+o(t).

Equations (12) or (14) prove the required lower response.
Normals away from the equality directions have a fixed positive
own-cap gap. Vertical caps were already included in (8).
No assumed rate of normal convergence is used.

For the upper bound use each exact canonical normal. Its own
mass is Gamma V-t kappa v_i+O(t^2). Equations (13)-(14)
give the three upper scores in (11). This proves the asserted
pointwise response, including for varying convergent bounded
displacements.

## 5. The unique limiting optimizer and global selection

For fixed v_0, the minimum of the last two scores in (11) is
at most a+kappa v_0/2, with equality exactly when
v_1=v_2=-v_0/2. The first score

    P(v_0)=-kappa v_0+a j(v_0)

is continuous and strictly decreasing, whereas
B(v_0)=a+kappa v_0/2 is strictly increasing. They cross once.
Their intersection lies in c<v_0<0, where j is linear.
Solving there gives exactly (3) and L_*=B(v_0*).
Thus mathcal_L has a UNIQUE global maximizer v_*.

Use g+t v_* as a trial point for the lower bound on the maximum.
For an arbitrary maximizing sequence, (9) bounds its displacement.
Every convergent subsequence has, by the canonical upper bounds,
limiting coefficient at most mathcal_L(v)<=L_*.
The trial point gives the reverse inequality. Uniqueness of the
limiting optimizer forces every maximizing displacement to tend
to v_*. Consequently

    max_y A_6,t((q,y))=Gamma V+t L_*+o(t).

The seven-base exact global reduction gives

    D_t=Gamma V+max{ta,ta,
                    ta+max_y A_6,t((q,y))-Gamma V}.

Since L_*>0, the third term wins strictly for sufficiently small
t. All global maximizers therefore have base q, and (10)
transfers their displacement and value, proving (3)-(5).
At the original g, the coefficient is instead a+a/2=3a/2.
Since L_*>a/2, moving the continuous point strictly improves
the global depth at first order.

For completeness the seven integer bases are exact. Their hull
is the quadrilateral

    -1<=z1<=1, z2<=1, z1+2z2>=-1.

Its integer points are precisely Q,r_0,p,p'. The three added
bases are exposed. All continuous generators lie in T, so
the four core fibers stay T and the exposed fibers stay E_t.
The hull is full dimensional. The other two anchor maxima are
exactly Gamma V+ta, the (1,1) core maximum is Gamma V, and
the exposed added-base depths are at most ta. The finite
isolators and all-source upper cover proving those values
are the ones in Section 2 of the seven-base response note.

## 6. Rational calibration

Choose L=1/6,H=1. Then

    a=w=2/3, c=-1/2,
    v_*= (1/10,1/10), v_0*=-1/5,
    L_*=3/5,
    D_t=2/9+(19/15)t+o(t),
    D_t/M_t=1/9+(47/90)t+o(t).                      (15)

At the trial y=g+t v_*, take the canonical l_0 normal and zero
opposite pair shift. Its exact seven-base mass is

    2/9+(19/15)t+t^2/50.

For l_1 and l_2 use a saturated shift, including one added
endpoint and excluding the other. Their exact masses are

    2/9+(19/15)t+t^2/200.

All these original caps have finite base coefficients, strictly
exclude the other core fibers, and fully capture r_0. They check
the balanced first-order coefficients; they do not replace the
all-normal lower proof above.

The conditional weak law of E_t is the uniform segment
g+[-L,L](1,-1). Its lambda_0 marginal is the atom at 1/3,
whereas its other two canonical marginals are atomless.
The diameter of t^(-1/2)(E_t-g) diverges. Both failures of the
older regime hypotheses are therefore explicit.

The verifier ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_anisotropic_strip_global_depth_response.py
uses exact rational tail minimization on every quadratic
vertex-event cell, rational polygon clipping, and exact score
balance. The normal-limit and optimizer arguments are analytic,
not conclusions of a finite direction screen.
